coverage_notes: Swept across 8+ major angles: (1) foundational empirical capacity limits (Miller 7±2, Cowan 3-4); (2) cognitive architecture and multicomponent models (Baddeley, working memory structure); (3) cognitive load theory and instructional design (Sweller, Paas, van Merriënboer); (4) attentional mechanisms and bottlenecks (attentional blink, perceptual load theory, multiple resources); (5) visual perception and information visualization (Munzner, Tufte, graph comprehension); (6) external representations and sensemaking (Scaife & Rogers, Pirolli & Card); (7) UI/HCI design principles and cognitive constraints (Norman, Nielsen, progressive disclosure, affordances); (8) emergent intersections (RAG UI design, LLM context windows as working memory analogy, feature creep, graph visualization constraints). Deduplication performed across 50+ search results; tiering applied per domain rubric (T0 meta-analyses and foundational papers with 1000+ citations, T1 peer-reviewed and highly-cited papers from top venues and journals, T2 seminal textbooks and canonical author works, T3 high-quality design essays and practitioner resources). Notable gaps deferred: neural substrate specifics (fMRI/EEG mechanisms beyond working memory function), individual differences in capacity (genetic, age, clinical), fine-grained attentional control strategies beyond detection of limits, cross-cultural working memory differences. Primary authorities covered: Miller, Cowan, Baddeley, Sweller, Wickens, Lavie (perceptual load), Pirolli (sensemaking), Munzner (visualization), Norman/Nielsen (HCI design), Tufte (information design).

sources.title: The Magical Number Seven, Plus or Minus Two: Some Limits on Our Capacity for Processing Information
sources.notes: Foundational 1956 paper establishing the 7±2 capacity limit for immediate memory span via absolute judgment and span of attention tasks. Introduced chunking concept. Most highly cited paper in cognitive psychology. Published in Psychological Review 63(2):81-97.

sources.title: The Magical Mystery Four: How is Working Memory Capacity Limited, and Why?
sources.notes: 2010 seminal synthesis by Nelson Cowan establishing the revised capacity limit of 3-5 meaningful items in young adults, distinguishing between task-dependent span and the fundamental capacity constraint. Current Directions in Psychological Science 19(1):51-57. Open access via PMC.

sources.title: Working Memory Model (Baddeley & Hitch 1974) and The Multicomponent Model of Working Memory Fifty Years On
sources.notes: Original 1974 multicomponent model of working memory with central executive, phonological loop, and visuospatial sketchpad. Recent 2025 retrospective by Hitch, Allen & Baddeley in Quarterly Journal of Experimental Psychology reviews 50 years of research and refinements including episodic buffer.

sources.title: Cognitive Load Theory of Multimedia Learning (Sweller)
sources.notes: John Sweller's cognitive load theory foundational to instructional design, distinguishing intrinsic, extraneous, and germane cognitive load. 2005 Cambridge handbook chapter widely cited. Core principle: learning cannot exceed working memory capacity.

sources.title: Cognitive Architecture and Instructional Design
sources.notes: Sweller, van Merriënboer & Paas (1998) Educational Psychology Review foundational paper on cognitive architecture principles for instruction. Established connections between working memory limitations and instructional design practices.

sources.title: Multiple Resources and Mental Workload
sources.notes: Christopher Wickens 2008 Ergonomics article on Multiple Resources Theory showing workload depends not just on task difficulty but on competition for specific resource types (visual, auditory, cognitive, motor) with strong implications for multi-task UI design.

sources.title: Load Theory of Selective Attention and Cognitive Control
sources.notes: Nilli Lavie's perceptual load theory establishing that task-irrelevant distractors are processed only when perceptual load is low and capacity remains unused; foundational for understanding attention and distraction in interfaces.

sources.title: High Visual Working Memory Capacity in Trait Social Anxiety
sources.notes: Study showing visual working memory capacity of 3-4 objects established via change detection paradigm; documents individual differences and relationship to anxiety and attention mechanisms.

sources.title: Functional Imaging Reveals Working Memory and Attention Interact to Produce the Attentional Blink
sources.notes: fMRI evidence that attentional blink (failure to report second target in RSVP within ~500ms) arises from working memory encoding bottleneck. Demonstrates hard capacity limits under task interference conditions.

sources.title: Dual-task Interference in Visual Working Memory: A Limitation in Storage Capacity
sources.notes: Demonstrates that concurrent visual working memory tasks interfere at storage stage when total set size exceeds capacity; encoding and retrieval unaffected. Critical for understanding UI interference between simultaneous visual tasks.

sources.title: Resources Underlying Visuo-Spatial Working Memory Enable Veridical Large Numerosity Perception
sources.notes: Subitizing range (3-4 objects) constrained by visuo-spatial working memory capacity; accurate enumeration breaks down beyond this limit. Directly relevant to counting visible UI controls.

sources.title: Change Blindness and Inattentional Blindness
sources.notes: Jensen review distinguishing inattentional blindness (failure to notice unexpected objects) from change blindness (failure to detect changes); both reveal limits on attentional resource allocation and visual working memory.

sources.title: External Cognition: How Do Graphical Representations Work?
sources.notes: Scaife & Rogers 1996 seminal paper on computational offloading via external representations; establishes how graphical displays reduce working memory burden via spatial and temporal constraint. International Journal of Human Computer Studies 45:185-213.

sources.title: A Functional Model of Sensemaking in a Neurocognitive Architecture
sources.notes: Pirolli & Card functional model of sensemaking via iterative foraging and synthesis loops; shows how external information architecture reduces working memory burden in complex analytical tasks.

sources.title: InfoVis: The Impact of Information Overload on Decision Making Outcome in High Complexity Settings
sources.notes: Study showing information overload (exceeding working memory capacity) reduces decision accuracy by 22-28%; demonstrates that visible information exceeding capacity limits actively degrades performance.

sources.title: Examining the Cognitive Processes Underlying Resumption Costs in Task-Interruption Contexts
sources.notes: Research on context switching showing ~23 minute re-engagement time and working memory overload via concurrent task loading; relevant to UI requiring repeated context shifts.

sources.title: Visualization Analysis & Design
sources.notes: Tamara Munzner foundational textbook (2014, CRC Press) on visualization design with 2500+ citations. Framework for analyzing visualization idioms including perceptual and cognitive capacity limitations in mark-channel encoding.

sources.title: Edward Tufte: Information Design and Visual Perception
sources.notes: Edward Tufte seminal works on information design (1983 'Visual Display of Quantitative Information', 1990 'Envisioning Information') establishing cognitive principles for effective visualization within human perceptual and memory constraints.

sources.title: 10 Usability Heuristics for User Interface Design
sources.notes: Don Norman & Nielsen foundational usability heuristics emphasizing visibility, feedback, constraint, and recognition over recall—principles derived from working memory limitations. Visibility heuristic directly addresses control density.

sources.title: Spatial Memory: Why It Matters for UX Design
sources.notes: Nielsen Norman Group article on spatial memory in UI design; explains how visual/spatial organization reduces working memory burden by supporting recognition-based navigation.

sources.title: Progressive Disclosure in UX Design
sources.notes: Progressive disclosure introduced by Nielsen 1995 as core pattern for managing cognitive load via gradual information revelation. Directly addresses working memory constraints by reducing simultaneous visible controls.

sources.title: Gestalt Principles: Understanding Visual Perception in Design
sources.notes: Gestalt psychology principles (proximity, similarity, closure, continuance) for reducing cognitive effort in visual perception. Early 20th-century perceptual grouping laws showing how brain minimizes working memory load via pattern recognition.

sources.title: Daniel Kahneman: Cognitive Bias and Decision Making
sources.notes: Kahneman & Tversky dual-process theory (System 1 fast/intuitive, System 2 slow/deliberate) showing working memory limitations force reliance on heuristics. Foundation for understanding UI cognitive biases under load.

sources.title: A Measurement Model for Visual Complexity in HCI: Focusing on Visual Elements in Mobile GUI Design
sources.notes: Recent empirical study measuring visual complexity via element count and spatial distribution; establishes relationship between visible controls and cognitive load in mobile UIs.

sources.title: Evaluating Information Visualizations with Working Memory Metrics
sources.notes: Establishes working memory metrics as objective measure for evaluating visualization effectiveness; shows relationship between verbal and visual working memory capacity and chart type preference.

sources.title: A Survey of Perception-Based Visualization Studies by Task
sources.notes: Comprehensive survey of perception research in visualization; documents perceptual and cognitive capacity constraints including working memory limits on task performance in visualizations.

sources.title: Matrices or Node-Link Diagrams: Which Visual Representation is Better for Visualising Connectivity Models?
sources.notes: ACM paper comparing node-link diagrams vs. adjacency matrices for graph comprehension; documents working memory demands of tracking edge relationships under increasing density.

sources.title: Exploring the Limits of Complexity: A Survey of Empirical Studies on Graph Visualisation
sources.notes: Comprehensive survey of empirical limits on graph visualization comprehension; documents cognitive capacity thresholds for node count, edge crossing, and visual complexity.

sources.title: Visual Working Memory Simultaneously Guides Facilitation and Inhibition During Visual Search
sources.notes: Study showing working memory content actively guides attention in visual search via feature matching; demonstrates interaction between memory and visual attention in complex displays.

sources.title: Feature Creep in Software Development – Avoid Common Pitfalls
sources.notes: Practitioner analysis showing 30-50% of software features provide marginal value; feature bloat directly increases UI control density beyond working memory capacity, reducing usability.

sources.title: RAG+: Enhancing Retrieval-Augmented Generation with Application-Aware Reasoning
sources.notes: arXiv 2506 on RAG system architecture; documents UI as key component (GROUSER framework) with emerging focus on cognitive load across retrieval, synthesis, and user interaction.

sources.title: Working Memory in LLMs: Context Window Deep Dive
sources.notes: Contemporary analysis drawing explicit analogy between LLM context windows and human working memory capacity; cites Baddeley & Hitch model as theoretical foundation for understanding token limits.

sources.title: Cognitive Load in Web Interface Design: A Study Based on Visual Complexity and Task Difficulty
sources.notes: Empirical study measuring cognitive load via visual complexity and task difficulty factors; establishes quantifiable relationship between interface element density and working memory demands.

sources.title: A Bottleneck Model of Set-Specific Capture
sources.notes: PLOS ONE paper showing attentional bottleneck limiting simultaneous processing of information sets; demonstrates capacity-limited mechanism independent of stimulus encoding/retrieval.

sources.title: Schema Theory: How Learners Organise Knowledge
sources.notes: Foundation for understanding how working memory interacts with long-term memory schemas; Bartlett & Rumelhart established chunking via prior knowledge reduces memory load.

sources.title: Visibility of System Status (Usability Heuristic #1)
sources.notes: Nielsen heuristic on visibility as core design principle; directly derived from working memory limitations requiring continuous feedback and visible system state.

sources.title: The Keyhole Effect: Why Chat Interfaces Fail at Data Analysis
sources.notes: arXiv 2602 paper directly addressing working memory constraints in UI; shows sequential chat interface (one-control-at-a-time) vs. simultaneous visibility trade-offs in data visualization tasks.

sources.title: The Cognitive Divergence: AI Context Windows, Human Attention Decline, and the Delegation Feedback Loop
sources.notes: arXiv 2603 examining divergence between LLM context window growth and human working memory capacity in AI-UI delegation patterns; directly relevant to RAG/agent-builder UI design.

sources.title: Eye of the Beholder: Towards Measuring Visualization Complexity
sources.notes: arXiv 2512 paper proposing computational measures of visualization complexity; addresses relationship between objective visual features and subjective cognitive load.

sources.title: User Mental Models in Interface Design
sources.notes: ScienceDirect overview of mental models in UX; explains how interface design must align with user's limited working memory model to reduce cognitive gap.

sources.title: Saliency, Attention, and Visual Search: An Information Theoretic Approach
sources.notes: Journal of Vision paper on saliency and attention mechanisms; documents how stimulus salience captures limited attentional resources independently of task goals.
